minutes.headline: Parks Commission picked three of four OPM firms to interview, in person if the senior center works, and left the Town Meeting field-closure idea alone.
minutes.summary: The commission got facilities and recreation updates, planned Earth Day cleanups and a volunteer day to pull up the carpet at a park building, and talked about whether to close parks fields on Town Meeting Saturday. Most of the meeting was spent on the owner's project manager (OPM) selection: interview format, then each member's scoring of four proposals. They agreed to invite the three top-scoring firms and drop the fourth. No formal votes were taken except adjournment.

budget_items.what_was_said: Members scored four OPM firms on a rubric; totals were read aloud and three firms ranked clearly above the fourth. The reference check category was left blank for now.

The invitation for bids for landscaping went to the procurement officer to be put into proper format.
A member mentioned the potential override and long budget meetings as the reason for raising the Town Meeting field closure question.
Three of the lifeguards are not returning. A member suggested hiring three to backfill, and the director is gathering hours availability.

Interview format: about 15 minutes of presentation and 15 of Q&A per firm, park-focused, with proposed staff attending and presentations supplied on a flash drive or hard copies.
The reference check score is left blank for now and used only as a tiebreaker if needed.
No vote was taken on closing parks properties on Town Meeting Saturday; the chair moved on after discussion.
Volunteer crew to pull up carpet and subfloor at a park building is aimed at Saturday April 6th, weather permitting, with the sign-up sheet planned for early next week.
January 17th minutes were not approved; members passed on them to read first.
